page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.16-64 is a flexible compute virtual machine instance configured with 32 vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, with simultaneous multithreading delivering two threads per core. The resource allocation yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU (or 4.0 GB per physical core).

Architecturally, VM.Standard.E6.Flex.16-64 does not include local NVMe storage, meaning that all persistent and non-volatile storage must be attached remotely via block volumes or network-attached file systems. The instance also features zero hardware accelerators or discrete GPUs. For network connectivity, the instance comes provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address alongside standard virtual cloud network interfaces.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory footprint positions this configuration for compute-intensive tasks rather than memory-heavy or storage-bound applications. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores deliver consistent instruction throughput for multithreaded workloads that do not require massive in-memory caching. Cost efficiency stems from the balanced, compute-forward resource density, avoiding unnecessary memory overhead.

Appropriate workload fits include continuous integration and build pipelines, CPU-bound batch processing, computational simulation, distributed microservices, application servers, and web serving where persistent storage is abstracted to remote networked storage.
